title: Spicy Peanut Noodles
description: Cold or warm noodles drenched in a creamy, spicy peanut sauce with lime, garlic, and ginger. The kind of thing you'll start craving at 2pm on a Tuesday.

steps.text: Cook the noodles according to package directions until just tender. Drain, rinse under cold water until completely cool, and drain well again.
steps.tip: Rinsing stops the cooking and washes off excess starch so the noodles stay slippery, not gummy.

steps.text: While the noodles cook, whisk together the peanut butter, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, sriracha, lime juice, maple syrup, garlic, and ginger in a large bowl until smooth. If the sauce is too thick to toss, thin it with warm water, a tablespoon at a time, until pourable.
steps.tip: Natural peanut butter can be stubborn. A few tablespoons of warm water usually loosens it right up.

steps.text: Add the cooled noodles to the bowl and toss until every strand is coated in sauce.
Divide among bowls and top with sliced cucumbers, scallions, chopped peanuts, and cilantro. Serve with lime wedges.
steps.tip: These keep well in the fridge for a day or two — just add a splash of water when reheating, since the noodles absorb the sauce as they sit.
